- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.33), model often underestimates or overshoots mid-cycle; apply mean reversion to 10–15 day moving average.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at +2–4% above true for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 5 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 2–3 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts in early periods when sentiment is positive; apply 1–3% downward bias to first 5–7 forecast points.
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.67/1.00 patterns, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day weighted average) to forecast.
